item.title: "Only elegant ladies allowed": a gym's rule in South Korea shines light on discriminatory practices
item.description: A gym in South Korea has ignited a nationwide controversy by displaying a sign banning "ajumma" (aunties) from using its facilities. The lack of anti-discrimination laws in the country permits organizations to implement such exclusionary policies.

item.title: World newsletter June 24, 2024
item.description: A recap of international news stories by Newsendip: a "blouse tax" in Brazil, the challenge of energy supply in tech, access to abortion in Italy, and more.

item.title: In Poland, a judicial review creates a constitutional crisis
item.description: Poland's Constitutional Court has ruled that a bill was passed unconstitutionally because two politicians, who had lost their parliamentary seats due to criminal convictions, were excluded from the parliamentary process.

item.title: Strawberries in Sweden and the shadow of one of Europe's deadliest gangs
item.description: The illegal sale of strawberries in Sweden has been linked to a sophisticated network of organized crime, with top gang members allegedly using strawberry stands to launder money.

item.title: Japan's donation-based local tax system goes off the rails
item.description: Japan's Ministry of the Interior and Communications announced on June 25 that it would review the rules governing local taxes, based on a system of donations to the city of one's choice.

item.title: 6,000 euros bonus for buying an electric car and helping a struggling German automotive industry?
item.description: During an online "automotive summit" on September 23, Federal Minister of Economy Robert Habeck, automakers, associations, and unions sought solutions to the crisis facing the German automotive industry.

item.title: Type 1 diabetes: A patient cured thanks to cellular therapy in China
item.description: Chinese scientists have managed to reverse type 1 diabetes in a patient thanks to a stem cell transplant, marking a significant advance in the treatment of this disease.

item.title: Spotify not essential to society to justify night work in Sweden
item.description: A Swedish court has denied Spotify the right to have employees work night shifts to maintain its audio streaming platform, ruling that the company's services are not essential enough to society to warrant an exception to the country's night work ban.

item.title: A third of a 70,000-person Argentine city falls for an alleged cryptocurrency scam
item.description: Alleged scammers used a trading platform that offered residents of the Argentine city of San Pedro the opportunity to double their investment in dollars in a month and a half.

item.title: Liberalization of alcohol sales in Sweden: The Systembolaget monopoly at risk?
item.description: A bill presented by the Swedish government proposes to modify the state monopoly on alcohol sales to support small local producers. However, before it can be adopted, this controversial plan, caught between divergent economic and health interests, must receive approval from Brussels and the EU member states.
